It is NOT the same company as Chagee Holdings (brand 霸王茶姬, NASDAQ: CHA), which is a separate, higher-end Chinese tea chain and a direct competitor — a distinction worth flagging given this project's history of HKEX ticker mix-ups. ChaPanda IPO'd on HKEX main board (stock code 2555) on 23 April 2024, incorporated in Sichuan, PRC, reports in RMB, December fiscal year-end.
overview: ChaPanda is one of China's largest franchise-driven freshly-made tea drink chains, ranked third in China's freshly-made tea beverage market by retail sales (Frost & Sullivan: ~6.8% share in 2023) behind Mixue and Guming. The group operates an almost entirely franchised store network (8,778 franchised stores vs. 13 self-operated flagship stores as of mid-2026, out of 8,863 total, including 72 overseas), and monetizes primarily by selling tea leaves, dairy, fruit, packaging and equipment to its franchisees rather than through royalties. Headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, it is expanding store density in lower-tier Chinese cities, building an overseas footprint (72 stores across 13 countries including South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, France, Spain, the US and newly Canada/New Zealand/Vietnam), and has recently begun pushing into freshly-brewed coffee as a second product category.

business_model.summary: ChaPanda earns the large majority of revenue from selling raw materials, packaging and store equipment to its franchisees (not from retail tea sales directly), supplemented by a smaller and declining royalty/franchising fee stream (upfront fees, ongoing royalties, training fees) and other revenue (design services, online delivery platform management fees, and a handful of self-operated flagship stores). This is a capital-light, high-volume supply-chain model: the company's economics are tied to franchisee store count and per-store sales/order volume (which drive ingredient and equipment purchases) rather than to owning real estate or labor at the store level. Revenue is largely transactional/recurring at the aggregate network level (repeat ingredient orders) but not contractually recurring per se; franchise fees are more one-off/renewal-based.

revenue_streams.name: Sale of goods and equipment to franchisees
revenue_streams.description: Tea leaves, dairy, fruit, packaging materials and store equipment sold to the franchise network, plus third-party sales of biodegradable packaging via 67%-owned Senmian New Materials; FY2025 RMB5,120.8m (+10.1% YoY), H1 2026 RMB2,523.6m (+7.0% YoY)

revenue_streams.name: Royalty and franchising fees
revenue_streams.description: Non-refundable upfront initial fees, ongoing royalty income, and pre-opening training fees paid by franchisees; FY2025 RMB191.7m (-10.2% YoY), H1 2026 RMB81.0m (-19.5% YoY) — the decline reflects both slower net new-store growth and competitive/fee-concession pressure to retain and attract franchisees

revenue_streams.name: Other revenue
revenue_streams.description: Design services to franchised stores, online delivery-platform operation/management services, and revenue from the 13 self-operated ChaPanda flagship stores; FY2025 RMB82.7m (+58.3% YoY), H1 2026 RMB50.1m (+22.0% YoY)

business_model.customer_type: B2B (franchisees) is the direct revenue-paying customer; end consumers are B2C tea/coffee drinkers reached indirectly through the franchise network. ~6,038 franchisees operating 8,778 franchised stores as of 30 June 2026, plus 13 company-operated flagship/showcase stores and 72 overseas stores (mix of franchise/company-operated by market).
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly Chinese mainland (8,791 of 8,863 total stores as of mid-2026, ~99.2%), spread across city tiers (new first-tier ~25%, second-tier ~20%, third-tier ~19%, fourth-tier-and-below ~27%, first-tier ~9%), with an emerging overseas segment (72 stores, +243% YoY off a small base) led by South Korea (32 stores, the largest overseas market), Malaysia (9), Singapore (7), plus recent entries into France, Spain, the US (Flushing, Queens), Canada, New Zealand and Vietnam.

main_competitors: Mixue Bingcheng (ice cream & tea, HKEX-listed, market leader)
CHAGEE Holdings (premium tea chain, NASDAQ: CHA)
Luckin Coffee and Starbucks China (adjacent coffee category as ChaPanda expands into coffee)
competitive_position.market_position: Third-largest freshly-made tea drink retailer in China by retail sales, ~6.8% market share in 2023 (Frost & Sullivan), behind Mixue (~10%) and Guming (~6.9%); one of only a handful of HKEX-listed pure-play Chinese tea chains, alongside Mixue, Guming and Nayuki (CHAGEE trades on NASDAQ).
competitive_position.market_share: ~6.8% of China's freshly-made tea drink retail sales as of the 2023 Frost & Sullivan data cited at IPO; more recent independent share data not located in filings or web search as of this analysis date.

moat_factors.description: 27 warehousing and distribution centers nationwide (as of mid-2026) within an average delivery radius of under 200km, ~94-95% of stores receiving next-day delivery and twice-weekly-or-more deliveries; vertically integrated raw-material bases (whole-leaf tea in Fuzhou, packaging materials in Chengdu) and a 67%-owned packaging materials subsidiary (Senmian New Materials) provide some cost and freshness advantage, though competitors at larger scale (Mixue) likely have superior unit economics

182.7m-201.4m registered members, 18-year brand history, and an established base of ~6,000 franchisees with high renewal activity provide switching costs and a recruiting advantage versus newer entrants, though franchisee turnover is material (497 franchisees and 499 stores terminated in H1 2026 alone, against 612 and 669 newly enrolled)

Intelligent replenishment and smart-preparation systems deployed in over 8,000 stores, AI-driven automated inspection, and a site-selection/investment-attraction data system aim to improve franchisee unit economics and retention, a differentiator versus less digitized smaller chains

Zero bank borrowings and RMB2.96-3.56bn of cash on hand (2025-2026) give ChaPanda capacity to weather a prolonged price war better than smaller, more leveraged rivals, and to fund continued overseas expansion from internal resources

Dense store coverage supports brand visibility and delivery efficiency in China, but the freshly-made tea category has low switching costs for end consumers and minimal true network effects compared to platform businesses

weaknesses: Heavily reliant on continued franchisee recruitment and store-count growth for revenue (goods/equipment sales), making the model sensitive to a slowdown in net store additions or to franchisee profitability pressure that could choke off new enrollments

Royalty and franchising revenue has declined for multiple consecutive periods (-10.2% FY2025, -19.5% H1 2026), suggesting fee concessions to franchisees amid competitive and economic pressure, which compresses the highest-margin revenue line
Gross margin degraded in H1 2026 (30.0%, down 2.6pp YoY) explicitly due to profit-sharing/concessions tied to the new coffee rollout, indicating new-category expansion is currently margin-dilutive
Limited brand differentiation versus Mixue (lower price point, larger scale) and CHAGEE (premium positioning); ChaPanda sits in a contested middle tier vulnerable to being squeezed from both ends

Small, early-stage overseas business (72 stores) means international expansion is not yet a proven, profitable growth leg and could consume disproportionate management attention/capital relative to current contribution

History of a cancelled dividend shortly after IPO (July 2024, the 2023 annual dividend) on cited "external environment" concerns, which dented market confidence even though dividends resumed with the FY2025 final payout made in H1 2026

growth_drivers: Continued store network densification in lower-tier Chinese cities (fourth-tier-and-below stores grew 7.0-7.2% YoY, faster than the overall network), where competitive intensity and rents are typically lower

Multi-category expansion into freshly-brewed coffee: coffee machines installed in 2,700+ stores by H1 2026 (ahead of plan), 15 new coffee products launched domestically in H1 2026 alone, targeting incremental morning/daytime occasions and new revenue per store

Overseas expansion accelerating off a small base: overseas store count grew from 21 (mid-2025) to 72 (mid-2026, +243% YoY), with new entries into Canada, New Zealand and Vietnam in H1 2026 alone, following earlier entries into South Korea, Southeast Asia, France, Spain and the US
Continued product innovation cadence (117 new tea products and 520 new formulas added in FY2025; 62 new products and 246 formulas in H1 2026) to sustain same-store sales and transaction frequency

Supply chain investment (27 warehousing/distribution centers, rising next-day delivery coverage to ~94-95% of stores, fruit centralized-delivery coverage up to 91% of stores) lowering franchisee input costs and improving retention/profitability, which supports the goods/equipment sales model

Digital/AI tooling (automated inspection, intelligent replenishment, data-driven site selection) aimed at improving franchisee store-level profitability and reducing closures, indirectly supporting the core sales-to-franchisees revenue line

Large net-cash balance sheet (RMB2.96-3.56bn, no bank debt) gives optionality for M&A, accelerated overseas capital deployment, or increased capital returns (CICC projects a 60-80% dividend payout ratio over the next three years) without financial strain

business.risk: Intense price-war competition in China's tea-drink category
business.description: Rivals including Nayuki and HeyTea have cut prices below RMB20 per cup; Mixue's scale-driven low pricing (RMB8-20) continues to pressure the whole category; HeyTea reportedly froze new franchise sign-ups in 2026 citing the price war. Sustained discounting pressures franchisee margins, which flows through to ChaPanda's goods/equipment sales and franchise-fee revenue if store profitability and new enrollments suffer

Revenue is structurally dependent on a large, somewhat transient franchisee base; 1,218 franchisees and 933 stores exited in FY2025 (vs. 1,399 and 1,159 newly enrolled), and 497 franchisees/499 stores exited in H1 2026 alone; a sustained drop in new enrollments or acceleration in terminations would directly reduce equipment/goods sales growth

Down 10.2% in FY2025 and 19.5% in H1 2026, suggesting the company is granting fee concessions to retain/attract franchisees amid competition — a leading indicator of pricing power erosion in its highest-margin segment

business.risk: Execution risk on new categories and overseas markets
business.description: Coffee rollout is currently margin-dilutive (H1 2026 gross margin -2.6pp YoY attributed to profit-sharing with franchisees for coffee); overseas expansion into culturally distinct markets (US, France, Canada) carries real estate, regulatory, and localization execution risk with a thin track record to date (72 stores)
As ChaPanda pushes into coffee, it invites direct competition from Luckin Coffee (China's dominant low-cost coffee chain) and Starbucks China, both with deeper category expertise and scale

financial.description: Gross margin swung from +1.3pp in FY2025 to -2.6pp in H1 2026 as the company shared profits with franchisees to support coffee category adoption and likely to counter competitive pressure, illustrating that margins are a lever management actively trades off against store-network health

financial.risk: FX exposure on IPO proceeds and overseas cash
financial.description: IPO proceeds held substantially in HKD and some bank deposits in USD create translation exposure against the RMB reporting currency; the company does not hedge this exposure

The board cancelled the proposed 2023 annual dividend shortly after the April 2024 IPO citing 'changes in the external environment,' triggering a share-price decline; while the FY2025 final dividend was subsequently paid (reflected in the H1 2026 cash flow) and CICC projects a 60-80% payout ratio for FY2025-FY2027, the 2024 precedent shows policy can be revised on short notice

regulatory.description: Freshly-made beverage chains in China face recurring scrutiny over food safety, ingredient sourcing, and franchisee quality control; a high-profile incident at any franchised store could cause reputational damage disproportionate to the company's direct operational control, given it does not run most stores itself

PRC franchise regulations require specific disclosure, deposit and cooling-off provisions for franchisees; incremental tightening of franchise regulation could raise the company's compliance costs or slow new-store enrollment

As with other HKEX-listed mainland issuers, ChaPanda is subject to PRC outbound-investment and capital-control rules affecting overseas expansion funding, and to evolving HKEX/SFC disclosure requirements; the 2024 dividend cancellation was reportedly linked in press commentary to overseas fund-approval friction, though the company did not confirm this

New store openings in the US, Canada, EU (France, Spain) and other jurisdictions expose the company to local food-safety, labor, and import/customs regulation for sourced ingredients, as well as any Sino-Western trade friction affecting cross-border supply chains

macro.description: Freshly-made tea/coffee is a discretionary, low-ticket-but-high-frequency purchase; a soft Chinese consumer environment (property-sector drag, youth unemployment, cautious household spending) has been a central driver of the sector-wide price war and could continue to pressure same-store sales and new franchisee economics

Reporting (Goldman Sachs, mid-2026) suggests the delivery-subsidy wars among Chinese food-delivery platforms are winding down, which had been inflating order volumes across the tea/coffee category; removal of subsidies could soften volume growth sector-wide

Exposure to agricultural commodity costs (tea leaves, dairy, fresh fruit) and packaging materials; the company's scaled procurement and vertically integrated production bases partially mitigate this but do not eliminate it

macro.risk: RMB currency and PRC capital markets sentiment
macro.description: As an RMB-earning, HKD-listed issuer, valuation and capital-raising capacity are influenced by broader sentiment toward Chinese consumer/ADR-adjacent equities and RMB/HKD-USD currency moves

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's freshly-made tea drink market has matured rapidly post-pandemic and entered a phase of intense price competition and consolidation; multiple leading brands (Mixue, Guming, ChaPanda, Nayuki) have now listed in Hong Kong, increasing public scrutiny of unit economics. Growth is shifting from new-store openings in saturated higher-tier cities toward lower-tier city penetration and overseas expansion, while category extension (coffee) is a common strategic response to slowing same-store growth domestically.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - discretionary consumer spending exposure, but tea/coffee is a relatively low-ticket, habitual purchase that has historically shown some resilience versus big-ticket discretionary categories; franchise-fee revenue is more cyclically sensitive than staple ingredient sales.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (no bank borrowings as of FY2025/H1 2026); indirect sensitivity via Chinese consumer credit conditions and the broader PRC property/consumption cycle.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: RMB is the functional and reporting currency; HKD exposure from IPO proceeds and USD exposure from certain bank deposits are unhedged. The HKD listing currency (quote) versus RMB-denominated financials is a point of attention consistent with other HKEX-listed mainland issuers in this project's history, though no evidence of a currency-mismatch valuation error was found here.
key_input_costs: Coffee beans (new, growing input as the coffee category scales)
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: PRC food-safety, franchise-disclosure, and consumer-protection regulation continues to tighten gradually across the restaurant/retail-franchise sector; no company-specific adverse regulatory action was identified in the filings reviewed or in web search as of this analysis date.

recent_developments.event: Reported H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) revenue of RMB2,654.8m (+6.2% YoY) and profit for the period of RMB344.7m (+3.5% YoY), with gross margin declining 2.6pp YoY to 30.0% due to franchisee profit-sharing on the new coffee category rollout; royalty/franchising revenue fell 19.5% YoY while goods/equipment sales grew 7.0%. Global store count reached 8,863 (+4.7% YoY), including 72 overseas stores (up from 21 a year earlier). Cash and cash equivalents were RMB2,964.3m with zero bank borrowings.

Coffee category rollout accelerated ahead of plan: freshly-brewed coffee machines installed in over 2,700 ChaPanda stores by mid-2026, with 15 new coffee products launched for the domestic market during the period, as the company pursues a multi-category strategy to add daypart occasions (morning coffee) alongside its core tea business.

Overseas footprint expanded into Canada, New Zealand and Vietnam, bringing total overseas presence to 72 stores across 13 countries/regions as of 30 June 2026, led by South Korea (32 stores, the largest overseas market), Malaysia (9) and Singapore (7).

ChaPanda opened its first United States store (Flushing, Queens, New York) and its first European stores (Paris, May 2025), part of a broader push into East Asia, Southeast Asia, North America and Europe; management has publicly cautioned that domestic Chinese tea-brand growth rates cannot be directly replicated overseas and that building brand presence in markets like France requires long-term commitment.

Board approved audited FY2025 results: full-year revenue RMB5,395.1m (+9.7% YoY), gross profit RMB1,753.8m (+14.3% YoY, gross margin up 1.3pp to 32.5%), adjusted net profit RMB833.3m (+29.2% YoY), profit for the year RMB821.4m (+71.2% YoY, aided by non-recurring items in the prior-year base). Global store count reached 8,621 (+2.7% YoY) with continued deepening in fourth-tier-and-below cities (+7.0% YoY).

CICC maintained an "Outperform Industry" rating on ChaPanda, cutting its price target ~23% to HK$9.3 (from an earlier HK$12 target set around September 2025), implying roughly 31% upside at the time; CICC's FY2025/FY2026 net profit forecasts were RMB870m/RMB1.06bn, and it projected a 60-80% dividend payout ratio over the following three years, alongside expectations for ChaPanda to expand further into the coffee category in 2026 to boost morning sales.

The board cancelled the previously proposed 2023 annual dividend (HK$0.3069/share, ~HK$454m total) citing 'recent changes in the external environment,' with press commentary (unconfirmed by the company) linking the reversal to overseas-fund-approval issues; shares fell roughly 9-13% over the following days to a post-IPO low. The FY2025 final dividend was subsequently approved and paid (reflected in the H1 2026 cash-flow statement), suggesting the 2024 episode was a one-off rather than a structural shift away from capital returns.

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (28 August 2026); no formal numeric management guidance disclosed in company filings reviewed

items.target: 60-80% (per CICC sell-side estimate, not direct company guidance)
items.notes: This is a sell-side (CICC) projection rather than company-issued guidance; ChaPanda's own filings do not disclose a formal payout-ratio target, though the FY2025 final dividend was declared and paid in H1 2026, and the FY2023 annual dividend was controversially cancelled shortly after the April 2024 IPO.

items.target: Continued steady store growth, with emphasis on lower-tier city penetration and 'prudent' overseas expansion
items.notes: Management's FY2025 annual report and H1 2026 interim outlook both describe a 'steady' expansion strategy rather than citing specific net-new-store targets for FY2026; language emphasizes quality/profitability of store openings over raw unit growth given competitive intensity.

items.target: Continue systematic expansion of freshly-brewed coffee store coverage, product R&D and market promotion
items.vs_prior: accelerating (2,700+ stores already equipped by H1 2026, ahead of initial plan)
items.notes: No specific store-count or revenue target disclosed for the coffee category; management has flagged it as a 2026 strategic priority to diversify consumption occasions.

items.vs_prior: N/A - external estimate, not company guidance
items.notes: Actual FY2025 profit for the year came in at RMB821.4m per the audited annual report, modestly below the CICC FY2025 estimate cited in its December 2025 note (the estimate predated the final audited figure).

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Wang Xiaokun's FY2025 statement describes 2025 as a year of 'deep differentiation and structured adjustment' in China's freshly-made tea industry, with top-tier brands' capital-market entries reshaping competitive dynamics around product development, supply-chain scale and brand recognition. Management points to continued investment in upstream raw-material sourcing, warehousing/logistics and digital quality control as a 'core barrier against market fluctuations,' and frames overseas expansion and the new coffee category as the two principal avenues for diversifying growth beyond an increasingly saturated and price-competitive domestic tea market. The H2 2026 outlook in the interim report explicitly references 'external environmental fluctuations and industry changes' requiring flexible adjustment of business strategy, cost control and risk management — language that signals continued caution about the domestic competitive environment rather than an all-clear.

bull_case: Top-3 scaled player in a large and still-growing Chinese tea-drink category, with a debt-free balance sheet (RMB2.96-3.56bn cash, zero bank borrowings) providing resilience to outlast smaller, less-capitalized rivals through the current price war

Multi-category diversification into freshly-brewed coffee is scaling faster than planned (2,700+ stores equipped within roughly half a year), opening a large incremental addressable market (China's coffee category, led by Luckin's proof of concept) without requiring a new store network

Early but rapidly growing overseas footprint (72 stores, +243% YoY) provides a long-dated growth option in markets without the same intensity of domestic Chinese price competition, and the company has shown willingness to enter developed markets (US, France, Canada)

Deepening penetration of lower-tier Chinese cities (fourth-tier-and-below stores +7% YoY, now ~27% of the network) targets a less-saturated, potentially higher-margin segment of the domestic market than the contested first/new-first-tier battleground

Resumption of dividend payments (FY2025 final dividend paid in H1 2026) and a sell-side-projected 60-80% payout ratio offer a shareholder-return underpin if execution continues to normalize after the post-IPO dividend-cancellation episode
bear_case: Core royalty/franchise-fee revenue has fallen for multiple consecutive periods (-10.2% FY2025, -19.5% H1 2026), a leading indicator that competitive and economic pressure is forcing fee concessions to franchisees, eroding the company's highest-margin revenue stream

China's tea-drink sector price war (Mixue's scale-driven low pricing, HeyTea's and Nayuki's discounting, new entrants) shows no clear sign of near-term resolution, and ChaPanda's own gross margin already weakened in H1 2026 (-2.6pp YoY) partly due to profit-sharing concessions tied to the coffee push

The business model's heavy dependence on franchisee store-count growth and churn dynamics (roughly 500 franchisees exiting every six months) makes revenue structurally exposed to any slowdown in new franchisee recruitment, which is itself sensitive to franchisee-level profitability under price-war conditions

Entering the freshly-brewed coffee category pits ChaPanda against far more established, better-resourced competitors (Luckin Coffee's dominant low-cost scale, Starbucks China's premium brand), with no guarantee of profitable category economics given early margin dilution

The 2024 post-IPO dividend cancellation and associated share-price decline illustrate governance/communication risk and the potential for capital-return policy to shift abruptly if the 'external environment' (regulatory, competitive, or capital-flow) deteriorates again

Overseas expansion, while fast-growing in percentage terms, remains tiny in absolute scale (72 stores) and unproven for profitability; management itself has cautioned that China's domestic growth playbook does not translate directly to markets like the US or France
